title: GRADE reasons to rate certainty down
description: The five domains for which GRADE lowers the certainty of a body of evidence. Each rating-down is recorded with the code that caused it, so the grade can be re-examined. Moved from smart-kg/methodologies/grade.md by bean wg7r, 2026-09-24 (owner: 'needs to be part of skill/SKOS'). Read with the `grade` skill.

source.note: GRADE Handbook (Schünemann H, Brożek J, Guyatt G, Oxman A, eds.), section 5.2: factors that can reduce the certainty of evidence; GRADE guidelines 4-8, J Clin Epidemiol 2011

codes.label: Risk of bias
codes.definition: Limitations in the design or execution of the included studies — such as lack of allocation concealment, lack of blinding, or loss to follow-up — that make the estimate likely to be biased.

codes.label: Inconsistency
codes.definition: Unexplained heterogeneity: the studies' effect estimates differ widely, their confidence intervals overlap little, or statistical tests show heterogeneity that the analysis cannot explain.

codes.label: Indirectness
codes.definition: The evidence does not answer the question directly: the population, intervention, comparator or outcome studied differs from the one the recommendation is about, or interventions were compared only indirectly.

codes.label: Imprecision
codes.definition: The estimate is uncertain because the studies are small or events few, so the confidence interval includes effects that would lead to different decisions.

codes.label: Publication bias
codes.definition: Studies are likely missing from the body of evidence because publication depended on the direction or size of their results.
